title: Term Structure Schedule for the Operating Lines of Credit
content:
Every Operating Lines of Credit product runs for terms of a fixed length, takes advances only during an advance period at the start of each term, and either revolves or does not.

## Terms defined

- **Revolving**: true when principal repaid becomes available to re-advance during the term, false when every advance permanently uses the commitment.
- **Term**: the length of one term from the booking or renewal effective date to maturity, in calendar months.
- **Advance period**: the calendar months from the start of a term during which advances may be booked; the advance cutoff date is the start date plus this many months.
- **Renewable**: whether the product can be renewed for a further term (a seasonal loan is re-originated, never renewed).

## Schedule

| Product | Revolving | Term (calendar months) | Advance period (calendar months) | Renewable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| StartRight Operating Line | Yes | 12 | 12 | Yes |
| ExpressLine Operating Credit | Yes | 12 | 12 | Yes |
| Seasonal Operating Loan | No | 14 | 9 | No |
| Revolving Operating Line | Yes | 12 | 12 | Yes |
| Borrowing Base Operating Line | Yes | 12 | 12 | Yes |
| Agribusiness Revolving Line | Yes | 12 | 12 | Yes |

## Notes on the schedule

The Seasonal Operating Loan is the only product that does not revolve and the only one that is not renewable: its advances stop 9 calendar months into its 14-month term, a repayment never restores what an advance used, and when it matures a new loan is applied for. On the five revolving products the advance period runs the whole 12-month term, so the advance cutoff date falls on the maturity date.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a Seasonal Operating Loan whose term starts on 15 March has its advance cutoff date on 15 December of the same year and its maturity date on 15 May of the following year.
